title.narrative: Annual Output Results
Output Indicator

description.narrative: 1.1: Number of mobile legal aid desk/clinics established within and outside the greater Banjul area/ #% of cases handled through legal aid mechanisms segregated by age and gender 1.2: Increase nationwide awareness and sensitization program on rule of law, access to justice, human right SGBV 2.1: Number of community NGOs, Women Groups and CSOs partnerships established for advocacy and public outreach on community policing 2.2: Number of Police officers trained desegregated by sex, age. 3.1: #/% of justice actors having received training through the training centre 3.2: Number of justice professional trained on the prosecution of SGBV offenses desegregated by sex, age /legislation revised. 3.3: Number of Virtual Courts established/ case management enhanced 4.1: Established accountable strategic mechanism among the justice institution and justice sector reform to enable sustainable coordination.

comment.narrative: 1.1 Baseline: Existing legal aid framework, but no effective and coordinated legal aid service delivery across the country 1.2 Lack of citizens’awareness of legal rights on how and the available channels to seek legal support. 2.1 : Limited trust by the communities in the Police system 2.2: Limited capacity of Police personnel on community policing competent 3.1: Limited capacity within National Judicial Training Institute/justice sector 3.2: Capacities of government/CSOs on the prosecution of SGBV related offenses very low. 3.3: High case backlog 3.4: Limited Instruments for accountability, coordination and oversight within justice sector not implemented or non-existing

Established 8 mobile legal and 1 Prison Legal Aid Desk to improve access to justice service delivery, especially for women and children Strengthen institutional capacity of 5 justice institutions Launch of the RoL knowledge products, Strategic Plans and revised legislation to increase funding for the rule of law sector Increase community awareness on RoL and SGBV Strengthen coordination and strategic accountable measures among the justice Sector for effective service delivery

Increase access to justice and reduced case backlog by supporting Mobile Legal Aid Clinics in 16 communities and 207 (106 females, 101 males) including 39 children received free legal, mediation and social services. Also, 78 adult inmates (71 males, 7 female) received free legal consultations, 71 male and 6 female were granted bail, 1 female and 1 male case dismissed, 2 male cases withdrawn, 2 male acquitted, 1 released, and 6 convicted through the Prison Legal Aid Desks. In addition, upscale the capacity of 60 law enforcement prosecutors at the Police and Drug Law Enforcement on prosecution proceedings and supported the expansion of the virtual courts to the magistrate levels with 27 laptops resulting in 218 cases (190 civil, 28 criminal) being resolved.
To foster greater trust between right holders and duty bearers, as well as addressing security issues, upscale the capacity of 93 officers (70 male, 23 female) and 200 volunteers on community policing (CP), child & gender responsive policing, and had an inclusive engagement with key community members 161 (79 female, 82 male) in four regions Centre River Region (Janjanbureh), North Bank Region (Barra), Upper River Region (Basse), Lower River Region (Mansakonko, and Kerewan) identified by The Gambia Force Force as priority areas.
To enhance efficiency of justice service delivery and increase access to justice provided technical support on the revision of the Alternative Dispute Resolution Secretariat Acct and the revision of the Sexual Offenses Act, to align with international standards. Strengthened institutional structures through the development of the Gambian Bar Strategic Plan, CP frameworks, CP training manual and CP Volunteer Guideline.
Through launched of the Prison Assessment Reports, Judicial Strategic Plan and National Rule of Law Roadmap to mobilize resource for the justice and security sector.

Conduct publish perception survey and report evidence Increase access to pro-bono legal aid consultation, particularly for women and children inside and outside of Greater Banjul Increase community awareness on RoL, access to justice and security, human right and SGBV Increased capacities of government/CSOs institutions to improve coordination, monitoring and prosecution of SGBV related cases Number of prison personnel that received training on case and asset management

Public perception survey ongoing 86 (71 male, 15 female) received pro-bono consultation through the Prison Legal Aid Desk and the Mobile Legal Aid Clinics out of which 35 (30 male, 6 female) were granted bail. 2 Virtual High Courts established at the High Court. Resulting in 131 matters heard virtually, reducing case backlog. Increased nation wide awareness Rule of Law, Access to Justice, Security, Human Rights, Reforms, the Constitution, and the impact of COVID-19 on justice using national and community radio stations The Police Quarterly Crime Statistics Template developed and incorporated into the existing Case Management System and a Police Mobile App developed with 4 data collection tools/templates for the 4 most reported crimes aligned to the Criminal Procedure Code. 25 ( 16 male, 9 female) Police officers trained on the Case Management System and the Mobile App. The Mobile App was piloted at the Kairaba Police Station within the Greater Banjul Area. The CM and MA will facilitate reporting and evidence-based strategy design. completed GIS mapping of all Police posts, stations, district, and regional offices this will provide the GPF with the number of personnel, assets for fast tracking and decision making in resource allocation. Developed the ICT Strategies and established the official email and websites operationalization to enable effective communication and public access to information. Installed a Cell Tower to provide much-needed internet access to the Mile 2 Prison and the Prison Service Headquarters and facilitate inmates participation in the Virtual Courts. 25 Judges trained on the prosecution of SGBV related offenses that will arise from the TRRC recommendation. 23 personnel from the Judiciary, MOJ-SGBV Unit and NALA provided access to online legal catalogs to increase technical capacity and improve access to justice and service delivery. Revised the Evidence Act to improve cases prosecution Revised the Judicial Service Commission Regulation and the Judicial Strategic Plan to strengthen the institutions structure and operation system Developed the MOJ Strategic Plan to strengthen the institution structure and operation system Refurbished the sanitation facilities at Mile 2 to improve hygiene and sanitation. Completed two dormitories and raised the perimeter wall at Jeshwang Prison to address the urgent congestion and security to allow detainees more freedom of movement. 20 (10female, 10male) Prison personnel trained on case and asset management to facilitate reporting for evidence base strategic design The project has provided 23 personnel (13male, 10female) from the Judiciary, MOJ-SGBV Unit, and NALA access to subscriptions for online legal catalogs to further increase technical capacity.
